contract.purpose: Reverse-lookup registry of instruments. The point is not 'what does this script measure' -- the filename usually implies that, and usually implies too much. The point is `conditioned_on` and `cannot_answer`: what the instrument silently holds fixed, and which questions it is therefore structurally unable to answer no matter how many times it is run.
contract.rule: cannot_answer is mandatory and must name questions somebody could plausibly believe this instrument settles. An empty cannot_answer means the entry has not been thought through. Conditioning that is invisible in the output is the failure mode this registry exists to prevent: measure_anchor_recall applies the item cap before enumerating, so it reads as an oracle over placements when it is an oracle over placements *of the ten items the cap admitted*.

a single snapshot per invocation

whether the cap should be larger
anything about which item should have been chosen
whether recall matters: recall 0.167 with best_score_regret 0.0 was measured on one snapshot

scripts/build_branch_labels.py.note: The first instrument on this repository that produces a long-horizon paired label. Every earlier board-value label was short-horizon and is known unusable: placed-to-go is confounded by step and volume, immediate settle survival is unrelated to option counts, and 95.2% of Q-band sibling pairs tie on any short-horizon outcome.

tests/test_scenario_matrix.py.note: Audited 2026-08-03. Two assertions were weaker than their names: the pre-loaded test only excluded a placement within 1e-6 of a seated item's CENTRE (a 1 cm overlap passed), and test_two_containers_are_both_reachable asserted only that indices were in range, which passes when every action goes to container 0. Both were rewritten; the second was renamed because its docstring promised what it did not check.

conditioned_on: one episode per configuration -- n=1 per row, and the outcome is machine-speed dependent because the online policy's only stop condition is the wall clock

--trace is an INTERVENTION, not free instrumentation: NEDO_POLICY_TRACE_PATH switches on _record_item_lifecycle (agent.py:6740, consumed at 4101) inside the candidate loop and writes ~40 kB per decision, all of it inside the 6.5 s deadline, so a traced arm searches less. Traced and untraced runs are different arms and must not be pooled
the synthetic combinations built by build_scenario_matrix.py, hence the bundled 41-item mix across however many containers
outcome: terminal_decision (action source and candidate kind, --trace only)
cannot_answer: how well a configuration scores -- synthetic scenes, not comparable to the development suite or to any official number
which of two configurations is harder: the placed counts move by 2 or more between executions of the identical binary and config, and the death channel itself flips
which ITEM killed the episode or which item covered a priority one -- terminal_decision names the action's source and acceptance path, not the geometry that failed
anything about the 80-item two-container scale the rules describe for Task A
